ai.description: *Indirana paramakri* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It features a pointed snout and distinct, elongated, glandular dorsolateral folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana paramakri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad, dark-brown lateral band extending from the snout through the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Indirana paramakri* inhabits the rocky, high-altitude streams of the Western Ghats, typically found in moist evergreen forest patches at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Rocky-terrain Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky surfaces of its stream-side habitat at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana paramakri* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of approximately 150–200 eggs on wet, moss-covered rocks near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana paramakri* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting rocky stream environments at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The *Indirana paramakri* emits a high-pitched, rapid series of short, metallic chirps, typically heard while perched on mossy, wet rocks near cascading forest streams.
